sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: IRGC says two tankers hit mines; US weighs strike options as Trump says Iran is 'ready to fold up'

paragraphs.heading: Mine strikes claimed
paragraphs.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said two oil tankers, each carrying about 2 million barrels, caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, according to IRNA as reported by gCaptain and Modern Diplomacy. The IRGC said the ships had switched off tracking systems and used an unauthorized route; it did not name the vessels, their flags or any casualties. Early reports described only one tanker, and there was no independent confirmation. [[TAG:danger:unconfirmed]]

paragraphs.heading: Record attacks
paragraphs.body: UK Maritime Trade Operations said at least 10 vessels were attacked in or near the strait in the past week, CBS News reported, as attacks reached a record pace. CENTCOM's commander said the US naval blockade has kept Iran from exporting about $25 billion of oil. [[TAG:warning:shipping risk]]

paragraphs.heading: US options
paragraphs.body: ABC News reported that officials have prepared a range of strike options for Trump, including the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb. Trump has ruled out nuclear weapons and said he will not resume strikes before the November 3 midterms; CBS reported he said Iran is 'ready to fold up' and the US would win 'right after the election'.

paragraphs.heading: Tehran's line
paragraphs.body: Iran's parliament speaker said the country must prepare for war even while negotiating, and an army spokesperson said the strait would reopen 'if America leaves the region', according to CBS News and Fox News. Iraq's foreign minister said his country has lost about $60 billion during the war.

sections.title: Gulf, Yemen and Israel
sections.summary: Houthi campaign on Saudi Arabia grinds on; Israel heads to a deadlocked October 27 vote

paragraphs.heading: Houthi strikes
paragraphs.body: Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport and other Saudi sites have killed at least a dozen people, though outlets report tolls of 12, 13 or 17 for the deadliest strike, according to Al Jazeera and PBS. The Houthis also struck an Aramco administrative building in the Eastern Province, causing a limited fire. The Jerusalem Post, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported that many attacks rely on Iranian targeting intelligence; Iran denies this. [[TAG:danger:airports hit]]

paragraphs.heading: Saudi response
paragraphs.body: The Saudi-led coalition has struck Houthi-held areas, including oil facilities west of Sanaa, and said it intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait. The Houthis have warned the US against joining the offensive, CBS News reported. Iran's foreign minister, at a regional meeting in Baghdad, backed a 'political process' to end the Saudi-Houthi conflict, Fox News reported.

paragraphs.heading: Israel's election
paragraphs.body: Israel votes on October 27 with neither bloc near a 61-seat majority. A Maariv poll had the coalition and opposition tied at 52 seats, and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party is competing with Likud for first place, The Jerusalem Post reported. Opposition figure Yair Lapid said he does not trust Netanyahu not to launch an Iran strike that could disrupt the vote, The Times of Israel reported. [[TAG:info:Oct 27 vote]]

sections.title: Ukraine and the Russia Sanctions Waiver
sections.summary: Trump waives Graham Act penalties on Russia as Moscow pounds Ukraine's power grid

paragraphs.heading: Sanctions waived
paragraphs.body: Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving sanctions and tariffs under the Graham Act, including tariffs of up to 500% on Russian goods, just before they were due to take effect on October 18, ABC News, CNBC and The Washington Post reported. Trump told Congress the waiver serves the national interest; existing sanctions under earlier orders remain. It follows a temporary waiver on Russian diesel exports through April 2027. [[TAG:warning:sanctions eased]]

paragraphs.heading: Bipartisan backlash
paragraphs.body: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis called the move 'beyond irresponsible' and Rep. Don Bacon said the president is 'prolonging the war, not ending it', according to The Hill and Fox Business. Zelenskyy called the decision wrong and said he expects more sanctions relief to follow, CNBC reported.

paragraphs.heading: Grid under fire
paragraphs.body: Russia fired 332 drones and missiles overnight into Saturday, hitting more than 15 key power facilities in what Zelenskyy called one of the largest strikes on Ukraine's energy system, the Kyiv Independent reported. Regional officials reported seven deaths and about 90 injuries; Al Jazeera put the toll at at least eight killed. [[TAG:danger:energy strikes]]

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: France detains 1,200 in fuel-price protests; Pope Leo leaves hospital after lung surgery

paragraphs.heading: France in the streets
paragraphs.body: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said 1,200 people were detained after nationwide cost-of-living protests on Saturday, with 550,000 participants by interior ministry count and 800,000 according to the CGT union, Archynewsy reported. Earlier tallies put arrests at 166 by midday and about 400 later. Lecornu said 150 officers were injured. The protests are tied to fuel prices driven up by the Iran war. [[TAG:danger:1,200 detained]]

paragraphs.heading: Wider unrest
paragraphs.body: Euronews reported dozens of arrests as protesters clashed with security forces in Paris, and CNN reported police firing tear gas in several French cities. Cost-of-living protests also hit Belgium, Italy and Portugal, according to The Rio Times' European roundup.

paragraphs.heading: Pope Leo discharged
paragraphs.body: Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery to remove part of his right lung for adenocarcinoma, ABC News and NBC News reported. His surgeon said he could fully recover in about ten days and that nothing clinically prevents his planned trip to Latin America in November. [[TAG:success:discharged early]]

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies in Kentucky; early votes lean Democratic; press secretary exit reverberates

paragraphs.heading: Kentucky rally
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied at Northern Kentucky University on Saturday for House candidate Ed Gallrein and Senate candidate Andy Barr, saying the Iran war would end soon and that Iran will never get a nuclear weapon, CNBC and Local 12 reported. The Kentucky Lantern reported he tied a $100 million Defense Department investment in a Kentucky drug plant to Republicans keeping Congress, and repeated a promise of $5,000 checks if the GOP wins.

paragraphs.heading: Early vote signals
paragraphs.body: CNN reported early voting data showing Democratic advantages in Iowa and North Carolina, where registered Democrats outvoted Republicans by nearly 28 points on Thursday. Nate Silver's generic-ballot average shows Democrats ahead by about 8.9 points, and a Pew survey found Democratic supporters more motivated to vote. Early votes are a small fraction of the expected total. [[TAG:info:partial data]]

paragraphs.heading: Press secretary fallout
paragraphs.body: Katie Zacharia, forced out after five days, praised Trump as 'kind, wonderful, gracious', Yahoo News reported. Communications director Steven Cheung said she will move to a new role. Al Jazeera called her the shortest-serving press secretary in US history; no successor has been named. [[TAG:warning:post vacant]]

sections.title: Markets and Economy: Week Ahead
sections.summary: China GDP Monday; Tesla, Meta, Netflix earnings; record tanker rates squeeze Asian refiners

paragraphs.heading: China's data
paragraphs.body: China releases third-quarter GDP and September activity data on Monday. A Reuters poll of economists expects growth of about 4.4%, up from 4.3% in the second quarter but below Beijing's 4.5%–5% target range, and Caixin's survey points to a similar figure. Exports remain strong while domestic demand is weak. [[TAG:info:GDP due Monday]]

paragraphs.heading: Earnings season
paragraphs.body: Netflix reports Tuesday after the close, and Tesla, Meta, IBM and Texas Instruments report Wednesday, according to Earnings Whispers and Kiplinger's calendar. The Fed is in its pre-meeting blackout. Investors are watching whether tech results ease worries about AI spending after the Nasdaq's 4.5% weekly drop.

paragraphs.heading: Freight squeeze
paragraphs.body: The IEA said tanker rates for supertankers on the Gulf-to-Asia route reached about $36 a barrel in early October, more than five times prewar levels, and margins for Asian refiners processing medium sour crude turned negative in September, BOE Report and Hydrocarbon Processing reported. [[TAG:danger:freight 5x prewar]]

sections.title: Asia-Pacific
sections.summary: Takaichi's Yasukuni offering draws 'regret' from Seoul and criticism from Beijing

paragraphs.heading: Yasukuni offering
paragraphs.body: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering to Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine for its autumn festival on Saturday but did not visit in person, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. South Korea's government expressed 'deep disappointment and regret', according to Korea JoongAng Daily, and China also criticized the offering. [[TAG:warning:diplomatic friction]]

paragraphs.heading: Balancing act
paragraphs.body: Analysts quoted by The Rio Times said sending an offering rather than visiting appears designed to balance conservative expectations at home against the cost of worsening ties with China and South Korea, which have both been strained this month.

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Ebola now second-largest outbreak on record; Sudan's war spreads as hunger deepens

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: The CDC says the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is now the second-largest on record, with 9,235 confirmed cases and 4,444 deaths as of October 15, Contagion Live reported. Asharq Al-Awsat reported that Congo confirmed spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, bordering the Central African Republic. CBC reported that one in four deaths are children. [[TAG:danger:second-largest ever]]

paragraphs.heading: Sudan
paragraphs.body: The UN Security Council heard that 20 million people in Sudan face acute hunger, with famine risk rising in Darfur and Kordofan, UN News reported. Sudan Tribune reported five children killed in an army airstrike in North Kordofan, and the US extended its national emergency on Sudan for another year. Army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan vowed to retake 'every inch' of RSF-held territory, Al Jazeera reported.
